nodes.html: What happens when BAS is late
nodes.text: What happens when BAS is late

nodes.html: The ATO applies failure-to-lodge penalties for late BAS, plus general interest charge (GIC) on any net amount payable. Persistent non-lodgement can lead to the ATO issuing a default assessment (usually higher than reality) or escalating to garnishee action. Catching up voluntarily is almost always cheaper and less painful than waiting for the ATO to act.

nodes.html: How a registered BAS Agent helps
nodes.text: How a registered BAS Agent helps

nodes.html: A registered BAS Agent can prepare and lodge overdue BAS periods, reconcile bank and GST data for each period, request remission of failure-to-lodge penalties where mitigating circumstances exist, and negotiate payment plans for any resulting debt. Agents often have extended lodgement deadlines, which can buy time on current periods.

nodes.html: If you are several quarters (or years) behind, the matched BAS Agent works through the backlog methodically — reconstructing transactions where records are incomplete, coding GST correctly for each period, and lodging in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement, so engaging an agent early is the right move.

Most late-BAS problems are record-keeping problems, not tax problems. Fix the process and the lodgements take care of themselves.

nodes.q: What happens if I lodge my BAS late?
nodes.a: The ATO applies failure-to-lodge penalties (scaling with lateness and entity size), general interest charge (GIC) on any net amount payable, and may issue a default assessment. Persistent non-lodgement can lead to garnishee action. Catching up voluntarily is almost always cheaper than waiting.
nodes.aText: The ATO applies failure-to-lodge penalties (scaling with lateness and entity size), general interest charge (GIC) on any net amount payable, and may issue a default assessment. Persistent non-lodgement can lead to garnishee action. Catching up voluntarily is almost always cheaper than waiting.

nodes.q: Can I lodge multiple overdue BAS periods at once?
nodes.a: Yes. The matched BAS Agent works through the backlog period by period, reconciling transactions and coding GST correctly for each, then lodging in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement.
nodes.aText: Yes. The matched BAS Agent works through the backlog period by period, reconciling transactions and coding GST correctly for each, then lodging in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement.

nodes.q: Can BAS late-lodgement penalties be waived?
nodes.a: Potentially. A registered BAS Agent can request remission of failure-to-lodge penalties where mitigating circumstances exist (illness, disaster, family crisis). Remission is not guaranteed but a well-prepared request improves the chances.
nodes.aText: Potentially. A registered BAS Agent can request remission of failure-to-lodge penalties where mitigating circumstances exist (illness, disaster, family crisis). Remission is not guaranteed but a well-prepared request improves the chances.

nodes.q: Who can lodge my BAS for a fee?
nodes.a: Only a registered BAS Agent (or tax agent) can charge a fee to prepare and lodge a BAS, under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009. All matched bookkeepers providing BAS services in our network have verified, current TPB registration.
nodes.aText: Only a registered BAS Agent (or tax agent) can charge a fee to prepare and lodge a BAS, under the Tax Agent Services Act 2009. All matched bookkeepers providing BAS services in our network have verified, current TPB registration.

nodes.q: Do registered BAS agents get extra time to lodge?
nodes.a: Often yes — registered agents typically receive extended lodgement deadlines, which can buy time on current periods. The matched BAS Agent confirms your cycle and lodges within the applicable deadlines to avoid further penalties.
nodes.aText: Often yes — registered agents typically receive extended lodgement deadlines, which can buy time on current periods. The matched BAS Agent confirms your cycle and lodges within the applicable deadlines to avoid further penalties.

nodes.q: How do I prevent falling behind on BAS again?
nodes.a: The matched agent sets up systems to keep you current — regular bank reconciliation, STP2-compliant payroll, automated reminders, and correctly configured software. Most late-BAS problems are record-keeping problems, not tax problems. Fix the process and the lodgements take care of themselves.

nodes.q: How quickly can a BAS agent start on my overdue periods?
nodes.a: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched BAS Agent will typically reach out within 2 hours to begin the catch-up process, or you can call for immediate assistance.

nodes.q: Will the ATO charge me interest on overdue BAS amounts?
nodes.a: General interest charge (GIC) generally applies to any net amount payable that is overdue. A registered BAS Agent can help arrange a payment plan and request remission of interest where mitigating circumstances exist. Acting early minimises the interest accrued.
